name: MindMeister
tagline: Collaborative mind maps, presentations, tasks, and idea organization

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Personal
tiers.limits: Unlimited mind maps; 2 attachments/map; 7-day version history

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited mind maps and attachments; unlimited version history

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Unlimited mind maps/attachments/history; team administration; SSO available by contacting sales

pricing.billingTerms: 6-month or annual billing; no month-to-month plan
pricing.hiddenCosts: Prices exclude VAT and can vary by region/checkout. SSO on Business requires sales contact; the six-month billing option is offered but its exact USD equivalent was not exposed on the accessible page.

verdictSummary: The visible mind mapping loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. MindMeister earns its keep through interaction polish, collaboration, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a browser-based mind mapping editor with drag, resize, connect, keyboard shortcuts, autosave, and SVG or PNG export.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whyPeopleStillPay: MindMeister: The shapes are easy; customers pay for low-friction editing, reliable exports, collaboration, and a canvas that never fights them.
ongoingBurden: Own geometry, selection behavior, undo, clipboard interoperability, export fidelity, accessibility, and browser performance.

priorArt.name: Excalidraw
priorArt.desc: Open-source diagram canvas with an approachable interaction model.

alternatives.name: AFFiNE
alternatives.desc: Mind maps live beside documents, whiteboards, tasks, and presentation frames; free cloud collaboration is limited to small workspaces.

facts.install: Hosted signup or desktop app; Docker Compose for self-hosting
facts.engines: Self-hosted AFFiNE AI can be configured with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and FAL credentials
facts.dataFormat: Local-first clients keep workspace data locally and sync to AFFiNE Cloud or the operator's server; self-hosting uses PostgreSQL, Redis, and persistent blob storage
facts.gapVsPaid: AFFiNE's mind maps have less mature automatic layout, styling, presentation, task integration, and dedicated mapping workflow than MindMeister.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted/desktop app installs cleanly; self-hosting is a multi-service Docker deployment that needs a domain, TLS, secrets, storage, backups, and AI-provider keys for AI features

alternatives.name: TeamMapper
alternatives.desc: Small, focused collaborative mind maps with a straightforward Docker install; public hosted maps expire, so permanence means self-hosting.

facts.install: Use the public hosted instance, or deploy its Docker Compose stack
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted maps and collaboration state live in PostgreSQL; maps export to JSON, Mermaid, SVG, PDF, and PNG; maps on the public demo are not intended as permanent storage
facts.gapVsPaid: TeamMapper lacks MindMeister's polished presentation mode, task handoff, templates, and durable managed workspace on its public hosted instance.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted demo has no install, but durable private use means Docker, PostgreSQL credentials, a persistent volume, backups, and usually a reverse proxy/TLS

alternatives.name: WiseMapping
alternatives.desc: A genuinely free hosted collaborative mind mapper with unlimited maps and useful imports and exports; tasks and presentation tricks are absent.

facts.install: Hosted signup, or Docker deployment connected to PostgreSQL or MySQL
facts.dataFormat: Hosted maps live in WiseMapping's service; self-hosted maps and users live in the configured SQL database; maps import/export common mind-map and image/document formats
facts.gapVsPaid: WiseMapping covers collaborative maps but omits MindMeister's integrated tasks, presentation polish, templates, and broader team-workflow features.
facts.setupBlocker: Hosted use is clean; self-hosting requires Docker and a database, and the custom public license requires a visible 'Powered by WiseMapping' notice throughout the user interface

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of MindMeister is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for MindMeister, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: React + TypeScript + Vite + IndexedDB.
Primary job: Build a browser-based mind mapping editor with drag, resize, connect, keyboard shortcuts, autosave, and SVG or PNG export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: large template libraries; high-fidelity import and export; presentation and enterprise controls.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
